newsitem.title: USA: Strong LME copper spread to lure more COMEX stocks.
newsitem.headline: Strong LME copper spread to lure more COMEX stocks.

text.p: The flaring cash to three months backwardation spread on LME will enable the London exchange's warehouses in the U.S. to suck in more copper from COMEX depots, dealers said.
This in turn will put more upward pressure on U.S. physical premiums as spot copper consumers compete with LME warehouses for metal.
"The shift in the arbitrage has certainly made it a little more expensive to pick up spot metal, no question about it," a producer official said.
Premiums were quoted a firm 2.75 to 3.00 cents over COMEX spot month, with higher quotes on small, prompt metal deliveries.
A dealer added: "If I had metal, I would not sell it as spot, I would deliver it to the LME warehouse."
But a second producer said there was not enough spot physical demand to cause a sharp spike in premiums.

The ability to withdraw copper from COMEX warehouses in Tucson and San Manuel was hampered in the first half of July by tight availability of trucks and rail as the red metal competed with fruit and vegetables for freight.

"If you took the incremental changes between the Arizona (COMEX) warehouses and Long Beach (LME) over the course of the last couple of weeks, they could probably be 25 to 50 percent higher than what they have been had those traders been able to support shipments in the way they wanted to," the second producer official said.
Heavy cash buying in LME Monday amid Third Wednesday pricing, widened the London backwardation to $227/$235 a tonne, up from $120/$130 at close of COMEX Friday.
The LME cash premium over COMEX spot July contract has now soared to 4.5 to 5.5 cents a lb to make arbitrage trading even more attractive, dealers said.

"There are currently on order another 15,000 tons or so to move from Arizona to California. That, of course, could change to zero at the drop of a hat with the arbitrage having been spread out as it has over the last several days," producer officials said. "But I don't see any reason why they (dealers) would not continue to capitalise on it (arbitrage)."

COMEX stocks have fallen from a high of about 50,000 short tons earlier in the year to 35,454 short tons, with most of the offtake shuffled into LME warehouses in Los Angeles and Long Beach, traders said.
Overall consumption in the U.S. is still strong, dealers and producers said, especially in the rod sector.
"We had a buying opportunity in the market and it probably still is," a dealer said.

A producer said the rod market continued to exceed the company's expectations, noting that the American Bureau of Metal Statistics said deliveries of rod through May this year were up 7 percent, year on year.
"This is a very substantial gain and far in excess of what we were expecting," the producer said.
Meanwhile Kennecott Utah Copper Corp said its recently restarted 310,000 short tons a year smelter was "ramping up quite nicely", but a spokesman declined to give any specific production figures.
"We have said we will reach capacity later in the year, and it's still anticipated that we will still do that," the spokesman added.
